preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and n <= 100 and m >= 1 and m <= 100
preconditions.description: The input values n and m are integers within the range [1, 100].

postconditions.expression: k == len(points) and all(0 <= x <= n and 0 <= y <= m and x + y > 0 for x, y in points)
postconditions.description: The output k is the number of points in the set, and each point (x, y) satisfies 0 ≤ x ≤ n, 0 ≤ y ≤ m, and x + y > 0.

postconditions.expression: all(all((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2 != int((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2) for x2, y2 in points[i+1:]) for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(points))
postconditions.description: For any two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in the set, the distance between them is a non-integer.

postconditions.expression: not any(all((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2 != int((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2) for x2, y2 in points2[i+1:]) for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(points2)) or len(points) >= len(points2)
postconditions.description: The set of points is of maximum size among all possible beautiful sets.
